texts.facts: 5. The present revision was admitted vide order dated 13.2.2020 and the revisionist was directed to be released on bail. 6. The facts of the case are that on 27.5.2002 at about 08:00 a.m. Food Inspector R.P. Gangwar while being on routine inspection with his team found the revisionist carrying 20 litres milk on his bicycle for human consumption and upon asking he states the same to be of cow milk. He then introduced himself and asked the revisionist for license to sell which could not be produced before him. On suspecting it to be adulterated he prepared Form-6 and then gave Rs.07.50/- and purchased 750ml of the said milk and kept in three bottles in equal quantity and sealed it as per norms. The said material was sent for analysis to the Food Analyst on 28.5.2002. Food analyst vide his report dated 24.08.2002 opined that the material was found to be having 31% less milk fat and 48% less milk solid not fat in it. The sample was thus found to be adulterated. Sanction from the C.M.O. concerned was sought after which the complaint was filed. The trial court vide order dated 03.10.2011 framed the charges against the accused/revisionist for offences under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) and 16(1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The trial in the matter started in which Makhan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33408790/ 2 R.P. Gangwar, Food Inspector, was examined as P.W.-1 and Rajiv Sinha, Senior Assistant, District Women Hospital, Pilibhit was examined as P.W.-2. The accused denied the prosecution case in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. It is stated that after sanction to file complaint, a copy of the complaint along with the report of food analyst was sent to the revisionist/accused on 23.12.2002 as per Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. The present revision has thus been filed before this Court against both the impugned judgements and orders.
texts.arguments: 7. Learned counsel for the revisionist has argued two submissions being that the notice under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been sent after about 4 months of the report of food analyst as the said report is dated 24.8.2002 whereas the notice has been sent to the revisionist on 23.12.2002 and the second argument as has been raised is that although the prosecution states of sending the report under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to the revisionist but there is nothing on record to show that the same has been received by the revisionist and as such valuable right of the accused/revisionist safeguarding his interest is violated. To buttress the arguments learned counsel has placed the judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Vijendra vs. State of Uttar Pradesh: (2020) 15 SCC 763 (para-14 and 15) and Narayan Prasad Sahu vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh: (2022) 1 SCC 87 (para-5, 6, 8 and 9). It is argued that although P.W.-2 states of sending the said report along with the letter of C.M.O. concerned to the revisionist vide registered post on 23.12.2002, the postal receipt of the same is Ex. Ka-17 to the records, but there is nothing on record to show that the same has ever been received by the revisionist. Further the said report and the letter of C.M.O. concerned has been returned back in the office as would be evident from the statement of the P.W.2 and the letter dated 24.1.2003 sent to Food Inspector for service of notice and report upon the accused/revisionist, which is Ex. Ka-19 to the records. It is argued that the Apex Court has, in no uncertain terms, in the judgement of Vijendra case (supra) held that failure of the trial court to take into consideration that no evidence was brought on record to indicate that the report which has been claimed to be dispatched, was actually sent or delivered for the purpose of further reference to the Central Food Laboratory, if the accused is dis-satisfied with the said report. It is further argued that even the trial has failed to take note of the said fact and also to record a finding that there is no evidence to show that the said report has been received at the end of the accused/revisionist but as per the evidence, the said letter was received back and thus no notice was effected. The said safeguard is provided to the accused under Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. It is argued that the present revision thus deserved to be allowed on the said two counts. 8. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer and the present revision. It is argued that the report, as per Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, was sent to the revisionist by a registered post but could not dispute the fact that the said report has been returned back in the office. Learned A.G.A. although fairly concedes that the report of public analyst is dated 24.8.2002 and the said report was dispatched on 23.12.2002 which is after about 4 months which is in Makhan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33408790/ 3 violation of Section 13(2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. He submits that the material was found to be adulterated and as such looking to the said fact, the present revision be dismissed.
